title: When an AI agent goes off the rails, file a bug to fix the documentation – then test the fix
summary:
Here is a mundane question that came up in an agentic coding session: How do I convert a select widget to a radio group? I was working on Bram, a desktop app that harnesses coding agents to a GitHub-backed workflow. Bram’s UI is made with XMLUI, a framework that wraps a simple declarative syntax around React and CSS. Agents using the XMLUI Model Context Protocol (MCP) server are instructed to prefer How To examples that provide verified working patterns. In this case Claude didn’t find one, fell back to the documentation for the RadioGroup component, and after a bit of fumbling figured it out. All good, right?

Nope. Claude should have found a How To and solved the problem immediately. The absence of that document was a bug, and this new How To document is the fix. This particular bug didn’t bite too hard, but the How To catalog is full of complex and hard-won patterns that agents can struggle to rediscover. To ensure that XMLUI is reliably learnable by agents, we continually expand that catalog.

How documentation becomes testable
